key_insight: Large language models can extract gross brain findings from autopsy narratives and help classify neurodegenerative diseases, with best performance for disorders that have distinctive macroscopic patterns like PSP and MSA.
clinical_relevance: This suggests autopsy report text may be a useful source of structured diagnostic information, but mixed pathologies such as AD-LBD remain harder to separate.
method: 5,613 Mayo Clinic Brain Bank autopsies across 7 diagnostic categories were analyzed.
A fine-tuned LLM converted gross descriptions into 39 semi-quantitative features.
CatBoost and a second text-based LLM were trained using extracted features plus age, sex, and brain weight.
evidence_signal: On a held-out test set of 562 cases, CatBoost reached 0.73 accuracy and 0.65 kappa, while the text-based LLM reached 0.75 accuracy and 0.68 kappa; both had 0.66 macro-average sensitivity.
watch_item: Results come from retrospective autopsy reports at a single brain bank, so performance may not generalize well to other institutions, reporting styles, or real-time clinical settings.
paper_title: Diagnostic Value of Large Language Model-Extracted Gross Brain Findings in Neurodegenerative Diseases
